docs.title: Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks for prek (also compatible with classic pre-commit).

Hook What it does check-symlinks-outside-repo Forbids symlinks whose target resolves outside the repository check-agent-files-tokens Keeps AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and friends under a token budget check-yaml-schema Validates YAML against the schema in its yaml-language-server header mdformat Formats Markdown with a shared mdformat plugin set

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Add the repo to .pre-commit-config.yaml and pick the hooks you want:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-symlinks-outside-repo
      - id: check-agent-files-tokens
      - id: check-yaml-schema
      - id: mdformat

Pin rev

Pin rev to a release tag rather than a branch name, so the hooks don't change under you. prek auto-update bumps it to the latest release.

Then install the git hook:

prekpre-commit 
prek install

pre-commit install

docs.title: mise-managed hooks
docs.text: Hooks for third-party tools don't have to come from their upstream hook repos. mise-managed hooks shows how to install the tool with mise and run it from a repo: local hook instead.

docs.title: Building these docs
docs.text:
mise run docs:serve  # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
mise run docs:build  # static site in site/

docs.title: check-agent-files-tokens
docs.text: Fails when an AI agent guideline file exceeds a token budget. These files are loaded into the agent's context on every session, so every token in them is paid for on every request. Keep them short and move details into files the agent reads on demand.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-agent-files-tokens
        # optional
        args:
          - --max-tokens=4000
          - --encoding=cl100k_base

Runs on the pre-commit, pre-push and manual stages.

docs.title: Checked files
docs.text:
Pattern Tool AGENTS.md, AGENTS.local.md Codex, generic CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/rules/*.md Claude Code GEMINI.md, GEMINI.local.md Gemini CLI .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md GitHub Copilot .cursorrules, .cursor/rules/*.mdc Cursor .windsurfrules Windsurf .clinerules Cline .<tool>/skills/**/*.md (e.g. .claude/skills, .agents/skills) Agent skills

Root-level and nested files (e.g. services/api/AGENTS.md) both match. To check other files, override files: in your config.

Hook definition 
- id: check-agent-files-tokens
  name: check AI agent guideline files token budget
  description: >-
    fails when AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and similar agent guideline files exceed
    a token budget (default 2500, o200k_base).
  entry: check-agent-files-tokens
  language: python
  files: (?x)(
      (^|/)(AGENTS|CLAUDE|GEMINI)(\.local)?\.md$
      | (^|/)\.github/copilot-instructions\.md$
      | (^|/)\.github/instructions/[^/]+\.instructions\.md$
      | (^|/)\.(cursor|windsurf|cline)rules$
      | (^|/)\.cursor/rules/[^/]+\.mdc$
      | (^|/)\.claude/rules/[^/]+\.md$
      | (^|/)\.[^/]+/skills/.+\.md$
    )
  types:
    - text
  stages:
    - pre-commit
    - pre-push
    - manual

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --max-tokens 2500 Maximum tokens per file (must be ≥ 1) --encoding o200k_base tiktoken encoding used to count

The default of 2500 follows Anthropic's advice to keep CLAUDE.md under ~200 lines, at roughly 12 tokens per markdown line.

Needs network on first use

tiktoken downloads the encoding file on first use and caches it (TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR). Offline with an empty cache, the hook fails with cannot load tiktoken encoding ....

The count is an approximation

tiktoken encodings are OpenAI's, not every vendor's tokenizer, but they are close enough for a budget.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$ prek run check-agent-files-tokens --all-files
check AI agent guideline files token budget..............................Failed
CLAUDE.md: 3120 tokens > 2500 (move details into on-demand files)

docs.title: Run manually
docs.text:
prekpre-commitDirectly 
prek run check-agent-files-tokens --all-files

pre-commit run check-agent-files-tokens --all-files

check-agent-files-tokens --max-tokens 2500 AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md

docs.title: check-catalog-info
docs.text: Makes sure the repository has a valid Backstage catalog-info.yaml at its root and fixes what it can: the schema header, metadata.namespace and the endoflife.date endoflife.date/products annotation. Like end-of-file-fixer, it fails the commit when it changed the file, so you review and stage the fix.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-catalog-info

Runs on every commit (always_run, no filenames) on the pre-commit, pre-push and manual stages.

Hook definition 
- id: check-catalog-info
  name: check Backstage catalog-info.yaml
  description: >-
    requires a root catalog-info.yaml with a schema header, metadata.name and
    metadata.namespace, and keeps its endoflife.date/products annotation in sync
    with the languages and tools used in the repo.
  entry: check-catalog-info
  language: python
  always_run: true
  pass_filenames: false
  stages:
    - pre-commit
    - pre-push
    - manual

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Fails when catalog-info.yaml is missing, does not parse, or has no entities.
  • Adds # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/catalog-info.json when the leading comment block has no yaml-language-server header. Pair it with check-yaml-schema to validate against the schema.
  • Every entity needs metadata.name; a missing metadata.namespace becomes namespace: default.
  • For Component and Resource entities the endoflife.date/products annotation (product@cycle,..., sorted) is kept in sync with the repo:
    • products are detected from files in the repo that git does not ignore (tracked and untracked) (*.py → python, package.json → nodejs, lockfiles → pnpm/yarn/bun, go.mod → go, composer.json/*.php → php + composer, pom.xml → eclipse-temurin + apache-maven, build.gradle(.kts) → eclipse-temurin + gradle, *.tf → terraform or opentofu, Gemfile → ruby, Cargo.toml → rust, deno.json → deno);
    • the cycle comes from a repo pin: mise.toml / .tool-versions first, then .python-version, requires-python, .nvmrc, engines.node, packageManager, go.mod, require.php, required_version, ...;
    • a pinned cycle that differs from the annotation is rewritten;
    • an unpinned product gets the newest non-EOL cycle, but only when it is missing from the annotation;
    • products the hook cannot detect (e.g. gitlab@19.3) are kept;
    • every product@cycle is checked against https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/<product>/.
  • API responses are cached in $TMPDIR/pre-commit-hooks-endoflife/. A stale entry is still used when the API is unreachable. The cache is only used when its directory is owned by you and is not a symlink; otherwise the hook runs without a cache.
  • A file that is already valid is never rewritten; when it is, comments, quoting and folded scalars are preserved.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$ prek run check-catalog-info
check Backstage catalog-info.yaml........................................Failed
- hook id: check-catalog-info
- exit code: 1
- files were modified by this hook

catalog-info.yaml: added yaml-language-server header
catalog-info.yaml: terraform-gitlab: added metadata.namespace: default
catalog-info.yaml: terraform-gitlab: updated terraform@1.15 to terraform@1.16 (repo pin)

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Description --offline off No API calls: repo pins plus any cached API response; unpinned products with nothing cached are skipped --cache-ttl 86400 Seconds an endoflife.date API response stays cached

docs.title: Run manually
docs.text:
prekpre-commitDirectly 
prek run check-catalog-info --all-files

pre-commit run check-catalog-info --all-files

check-catalog-info [--offline] [--cache-ttl SECONDS]

docs.title: check-symlinks-outside-repo
docs.text: Fails when a committed symlink points outside the repository. Such links work on the author's machine and break (or silently point somewhere else) everywhere else.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-symlinks-outside-repo

Runs on the pre-commit, pre-push and manual stages, and only on files git tracks as symlinks (types: [symlink]).

Hook definition 
- id: check-symlinks-outside-repo
  name: check for symlinks pointing outside repo
  description: forbids symlinks whose target resolves outside the repository directory.
  entry: check-symlinks-outside-repo
  language: python
  require_serial: true # one run: a single csv header / tree, not one per batch
  types:
    - symlink
  stages:
    - pre-commit
    - pre-push
    - manual

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The repository root is git rev-parse --show-toplevel (falls back to the current directory outside a git repo), with its own symlinks resolved.
  • Each symlink is resolved with a non-strict realpath, so link chains are followed and broken links are still checked.
  • If the resolved target is not inside the root, the hook reports the offending links and exits with 1. Clean runs print nothing.

Tip

Relative and absolute links are both fine as long as they resolve inside the repo.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
$ ln -s /etc/hosts hosts
$ git add hosts && prek run check-symlinks-outside-repo
check for symlinks pointing outside repo.................................Failed
hosts: points outside repo -> /etc/hosts

Run directly in a terminal, the hook prints a tree instead:

$ check-symlinks-outside-repo hosts
Symlinks pointing outside repo
└── 🔗 hosts -> /etc/hosts

Inside an AI agent it prints CSV:

file,target
hosts,/etc/hosts

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --format csv in an AI agent, tree on a terminal, plain otherwise Output format: plain, csv, table or tree

prek and CI capture hook output, so there the default is plain.

  • plain prints one path: points outside repo -> target line per link.
  • tree groups links by directory (📁) and shows each as 🔗 name -> target.
  • table is a two-column File | Target table.
  • csv has a file,target header and one row per link, for machine parsing.

table and tree fall back to plain when stdout can't encode their box characters and emoji (e.g. an ASCII or cp1252 console).

The hook counts as running in an AI agent when any of these variables is non-empty: CLAUDECODE, CURSOR_AGENT, CODEX_SANDBOX, CODEX_THREAD_ID, GEMINI_CLI, OPENCODE, AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID, CLINE_ACTIVE.

      - id: check-symlinks-outside-repo
        args: [--format=table]

docs.title: Run manually
docs.text:
prekpre-commitDirectly 
prek run check-symlinks-outside-repo --all-files

pre-commit run check-symlinks-outside-repo --all-files

check-symlinks-outside-repo path/to/link ...

docs.title: check-yaml-schema
docs.text: Validates YAML files against the JSON schema they declare in a yaml-language-server header, the same header VS Code and other editors use for completion. The editor and the commit check read the schema from the same header, so you only declare it once.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-yaml-schema

Runs on the pre-commit, pre-push and manual stages, on YAML files.

Hook definition 
- id: check-yaml-schema
  name: check YAML against its declared JSON schema
  description: >-
    validates YAML files carrying a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` header
    against that schema; files without the header are skipped.
  entry: check-yaml-schema
  language: python
  types:
    - yaml
  stages:
    - pre-commit
    - pre-push
    - manual

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Only the leading comment block is read. The header must appear before the first non-comment line, and files without it are skipped.
  • https:// schemas are used as-is. http:// schemas fail the hook.
  • Local schema paths are resolved relative to the YAML file, like yaml-language-server does.
  • Files are grouped by schema and checked with check-jsonschema, which runs once per schema.
  • Multi-document files (---) are checked document by document, and errors name the document (f.yaml[doc 2]::$.name: ...).
  • A $ref that can't be fetched or found fails the file with cannot resolve $ref.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/github-workflow.json
name: ci
on: push

$ prek run check-yaml-schema
check YAML against its declared JSON schema..............................Failed
Schema validation errors were encountered.
  bad.yaml::$: 'name' is a required property

docs.title: Options
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Run manually
docs.text:
prekpre-commitDirectly 
prek run check-yaml-schema --all-files

pre-commit run check-yaml-schema --all-files

check-yaml-schema path/to/file.yaml ...

docs.title: mdformat
docs.text: Formats Markdown with mdformat and a shared plugin set. It replaces the repo: local mdformat hook I kept copying between projects, where the plugin list had started to drift.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: mdformat

Runs on the pre-commit and manual stages, on Markdown files. Configure the formatting itself with a .mdformat.toml in the repo.

Hook definition 
- id: mdformat
  name: format Markdown
  description: mdformat with a shared plugin set (GFM, front matter, TOC, code blocks).
  entry: mdformat
  language: python
  additional_dependencies:
    - mdformat
    - mdformat-gfm
    - mdformat-mkdocs # admonitions, content tabs
    - mdformat-frontmatter
    - mdformat-toc
    - mdformat-config # json/toml/yaml code blocks
    - mdformat-ruff # python code blocks
    - mdformat-shfmt # shell code blocks, needs `shfmt` (or docker) on PATH
  types:
    - markdown
  stages:
    - pre-commit
    - manual

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plugin Formats mdformat-gfm GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables) mdformat-frontmatter YAML front matter mdformat-toc generated tables of contents mdformat-config JSON/TOML/YAML code blocks mdformat-ruff Python code blocks mdformat-shfmt shell code blocks

shfmt

mdformat-shfmt calls the shfmt binary (or docker), so install it, for example with mise use shfmt.

docs.title: Changing the plugin set
docs.text:
Setting additional_dependencies in your config replaces the list above, so repeat every plugin you want to keep:

- id: mdformat
  additional_dependencies:
    - mdformat
    - mdformat-gfm
    - mdformat-mkdocs # admonitions, content tabs

docs.title: Run manually
docs.text:
prekpre-commit 
prek run mdformat --all-files

pre-commit run mdformat --all-files

docs.title: mise-managed hooks
docs.text: An alternative to pulling hooks from their upstream hook repositories: install the tool with mise and call the binary from a repo: local hook with language: system.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• No clone, no build. An upstream hook repo is cloned and, depending on its language, built (golang), put in a virtualenv (python) or pulled as an image (docker). A system hook just runs the binary.
  • One version source. The tool version lives in mise.toml, so the hook, the shell, the IDE and CI all run the same binary. There is no second rev: to bump.
  • Faster tools. You can pick a native binary over a Python one, e.g. ryl (Rust) instead of yamllint (Python).

The trade-off: the tool has to be on PATH, which mise handles.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: <tool>
        name: <description>
        language: system
        entry: <binary>
        args: [] # flags the upstream hook would pass
        types: [] # or files: <regex>

#:schema https://mise.en.dev/schema/mise.json
[settings]
minimum_release_age = "7d" # don't pick up a release younger than a week

[tools]
gitleaks = "latest" # the tool the hook calls

Or from the CLI, which writes the same [tools] entry:

mise use gitleaks

A mise task runs every hook against the whole repo:

[tasks.pre-commit]
description = "run pre-commit hooks on all files"
run = "prek run --all-files --cd {{config_root}}"

Tools not on PATH

`language: system` needs the binary on `PATH`. That holds in a shell with
`mise activate`. If commits come from a GUI client without it, prefix the
entry with `mise exec --`, e.g. `entry: mise exec -- ryl`. mise then
resolves the version from `mise.toml` itself.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hook Tool Replaces gitleaks gitleaks gitleaks/gitleaks ryl ryl adrienverge/yamllint shellcheck shellcheck shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py shfmt shfmt scop/pre-commit-shfmt ruff ruff astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit ty ty mirrors-mypy, pyright terraform fmt terraform antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform terraform_fmt terraform validate terraform antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform terraform_validate tflint tflint antonbabenko/pre-commit-terraform terraform_tflint

docs.title: gitleaks
docs.text: Scans the staged changes for hardcoded secrets with gitleaks. mise installs the released binary, so nothing is built on first run.

docs.title: Replaces
docs.text:
The upstream hook uses language: golang, so pre-commit builds gitleaks from source on first run:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    rev: v8.30.1
    hooks:
      - id: gitleaks # or gitleaks-docker (Docker image)

It runs the same gitleaks git --pre-commit --redact --staged --verbose and reads the same .gitleaks.toml. Upstream also ships gitleaks-system, which expects gitleaks on PATH like the local hook below, but pins its arguments in entry. The local hook adds --no-banner and a size cap.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      # https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml
      - id: gitleaks
        name: Detect hardcoded secrets
        language: system
        entry: gitleaks
        args:
          - git
          - --pre-commit
          - --redact
          - --no-banner
          - --staged
          - --verbose
          - --max-target-megabytes=10
        pass_filenames: false

pass_filenames: false: gitleaks reads the staged diff from git itself.

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
gitleaks = "latest"

mise use gitleaks

Configure rules and allowlists in a .gitleaks.toml at the repo root, with [extend] useDefault = true to keep the built-in rules.

docs.title: ruff
docs.text: Formats and lints Python. Replaces ruff-pre-commit, which installs ruff into a virtualenv per hook repo.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-format
        name: Ruff Format
        language: system
        entry: ruff
        args:
          - format
        types:
          - python

      - id: ruff-check
        name: Ruff Check
        language: system
        entry: ruff
        args:
          - check
          - --fix
        types:
          - python

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
ruff = "latest"

mise use ruff

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
ruff reads ruff.toml, .ruff.toml or pyproject.toml. Set up a .ruff.toml at the repo root: it keeps ruff config out of pyproject.toml and works in repos without one. This repo's config:

.ruff.toml
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/
line-length = 120

[lint]
allowed-confusables = ["ℹ"] # emoji in console output
select =["I", "E", "W", "F", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4", "RUF"]

select turns on rule sets beyond ruff's default (E4, E7, E9, F); see the rules list.

docs.title: ryl
docs.text: Lints YAML with ryl, a yamllint-compatible linter written in Rust. It replaces the Python yamllint hook and reads the same .yamllint.yaml config.

docs.title: Replaces
docs.text:
The upstream yamllint hook installs yamllint into a Python virtualenv:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/adrienverge/yamllint
    rev: v1.38.0
    hooks:
      - id: yamllint
        args:
          - --no-warnings # report errors only

ryl is a drop-in replacement: same CLI flags, same config, no Python. Swap the hook for the local one below.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ryl
        name: Lint YAML
        language: system
        entry: ryl
        args:
          - --no-warnings # report errors only
        types:
          - yaml

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
ryl is not in the mise registry, so install it from its GitHub releases.

mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
ryl = "latest"

[tool_alias]
ryl = "github:owenlamont/ryl"

The alias keeps the short name in [tools].

mise use github:owenlamont/ryl

This writes "github:owenlamont/ryl" = "latest" to [tools].

To move to ryl's native config, ryl --migrate-configs --migrate-write converts .yamllint.yaml into .ryl.toml.

docs.title: shellcheck
docs.text: Lints shell scripts with ShellCheck. mise installs the binary directly, so the hook needs neither Docker nor Python.

docs.title: Replaces
docs.text:
The official hook, shellcheck-precommit, runs shellcheck in a Docker image:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck-precommit
    rev: v0.11.0
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck

shellcheck-py is the other common option and installs the binary through a Python wheel. Both run the same shellcheck with the same .shellcheckrc. Swap either one for the local hook below.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck
        name: shellcheck
        language: system
        entry: shellcheck
        types:
          - shell

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
shellcheck = "latest"

mise use shellcheck

Configure checks in a .shellcheckrc at the repo root.

docs.title: shfmt
docs.text: Formats shell scripts with shfmt. mise installs the binary directly, so the hook needs neither Python, Go nor Docker.

docs.title: Replaces
docs.text:
The usual upstream hook, pre-commit-shfmt, installs shfmt through a Python wheel:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt
    rev: v3.14.1-1
    hooks:
      - id: shfmt # or shfmt-src (Go build), shfmt-docker (Docker image)

It runs the same shfmt with --write and reads the same .editorconfig. Swap it for the local hook below.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: shfmt
        name: Format shell scripts
        language: system
        entry: shfmt
        args:
          - -w # rewrite files; use -d to only show a diff
        types:
          - shell

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
shfmt = "latest"

mise use shfmt

shfmt reads indentation and other options from .editorconfig, so keep formatting flags there rather than in args.

Note

The mdformat hook also needs shfmt on PATH to format shell code blocks.

docs.title: terraform fmt
docs.text: Formats Terraform files. Replaces terraform_fmt from pre-commit-terraform, which is a bash wrapper around the same command.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: terraform-fmt
        name: terraform fmt
        language: system
        entry: terraform fmt
        files: \.(tf|tfvars|tftest\.hcl)$

terraform fmt takes several files at once and rewrites them in place.

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
terraform = "1.16" # match required_version in versions.tf

mise use terraform@1.16

For OpenTofu use tofu fmt and mise use opentofu.

docs.title: terraform validate
docs.text: Validates every Terraform module that has a changed .tf file. Replaces terraform_validate from pre-commit-terraform.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
terraform validate works on a directory, not on files, and needs an initialized module. The entry turns the changed files into their unique directories, runs init -backend=false there (no state access, only providers and modules), then validates:

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: terraform-validate
        name: terraform validate
        language: system
        entry: >-
          bash -c 'rc=0;
          for d in $(printf "%s\n" "$@" | xargs -n1 dirname | sort -u); do
          terraform -chdir="$d" init -backend=false -input=false >/dev/null &&
          terraform -chdir="$d" validate -no-color || rc=1; done; exit $rc' --
        files: \.tf$
        require_serial: true
  • The trailing -- becomes $0, so the file names land in $@.
  • rc keeps going after a failed module, so one run reports all of them.
  • require_serial: true stops parallel batches from running init on the same directory at once.

Lock files

init writes .terraform.lock.hcl in each validated directory. Commit them, or the next init picks provider versions again.

docs.title: mise
docs.text:
mise.tomlCLI 
[tools]
terraform = "1.16" # match required_version in versions.tf

mise use terraform@1.16

docs.title: tflint
docs.text: Lints Terraform with tflint. Replaces terraform_tflint from pre-commit-terraform.

docs.title: Hook
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: tflint
        name: tflint
        language: system
        entry: tflint
        args:
          - --recursive # every module under the repo root
        pass_filenames: false

Goal: A prek/pre-commit hook check-catalog-info that requires a root Backstage catalog-info.yaml, adds the schema header and metadata.namespace: default when missing, and keeps the endoflife.date/products annotation in sync with the languages and tools the repo uses.

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import sys
from itertools import takewhile

import click
from ruamel.yaml import YAML
from ruamel.yaml.error import YAMLError

from pre_commit_hooks.util import project_dir

CATALOG = "catalog-info.yaml"
HEADER = "# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/catalog-info.json"


# --- catalog-info.yaml editing -----------------------------------------------


def split_prelude(text: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Leading comment and blank lines (ruamel drops comments before `---`) and the rest."""
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines) and (lines[i].startswith("#") or not lines[i].strip()):
        i += 1
    return "".join(lines[:i]), "".join(lines[i:])


def yaml_rt() -> YAML:
    y = YAML()
    y.preserve_quotes = True
    y.indent(mapping=2, sequence=4, offset=2)
    y.width = 4096  # never re-wrap long or folded scalars
    return y


@click.command()
def main() -> int:
    """Checks and fixes the repo's Backstage catalog-info.yaml."""
    root = project_dir()
    path = os.path.join(root, CATALOG)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: not found in {root}")
        sys.exit(1)

    fixes: list[str] = []
    errors: list[str] = []
    prelude, body = split_prelude(text)
    if not any(
        "yaml-language-server:" in line for line in takewhile(lambda line: line.startswith("#"), prelude.splitlines())
    ):
        prelude = HEADER + "\n" + prelude
        fixes.append("added yaml-language-server header")

    y = yaml_rt()
    y.explicit_start = body.lstrip().startswith("---")
    try:
        docs = list(y.load_all(body))
    except YAMLError as e:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    if all(doc is None for doc in docs):
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: no entities")
        sys.exit(1)

    dirty = False  # body re-dumped only when an entity changed, so valid files stay byte-identical
    for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
        if doc is None:  # empty document, e.g. a trailing `---`
            continue
        meta = doc.get("metadata") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not meta.get("name"):
            errors.append(f"document {i}: metadata.name is required")
            continue
        if "namespace" not in meta:
            meta.insert(list(meta).index("name") + 1, "namespace", "default")
            fixes.append(f"{meta['name']}: added metadata.namespace: default")
            dirty = True

    if dirty:
        out = io.StringIO()
        y.dump_all([doc for doc in docs if doc is not None], out)  # ruamel writes empty docs as `...`
        body = out.getvalue()
    if fixes:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(prelude + body)
    for message in fixes + errors:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: {message}")
    sys.exit(1 if fixes or errors else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

API = "https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/{}/"
PRODUCT = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.+-]*$")
VERSION = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*")
BAD_PAYLOAD = (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)  # malformed JSON or unexpected shape


class UnknownProduct(Exception):
    pass


# --- endoflife.date API ------------------------------------------------------


def cache_dir() -> str:
    return os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "pre-commit-hooks-endoflife")


def releases(product: str, ttl: int, offline: bool = False) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Releases of `product`, newest first.

    A cache file younger than `ttl` is used as is; an older one only when the fetch fails.
    Offline: any cache file, or None when there is none.
    """
    if not PRODUCT.match(product):  # the name ends up in a URL and a file path
        raise UnknownProduct(product)
    path = os.path.join(cache_dir(), f"{product}.json")
    cached = None
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            cached = json.load(f)["result"]["releases"]
        if offline or time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path) < ttl:
            return cached
    except (OSError, *BAD_PAYLOAD):
        pass  # missing or broken cache entry: refetch
    if offline:
        return cached
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(API.format(product), timeout=30) as r:
            data = r.read()
    except OSError as e:  # HTTPError and URLError are OSErrors
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 404:
            raise UnknownProduct(product) from None
        if cached is not None:
            return cached  # stale beats nothing
        raise
    result = json.loads(data)["result"]["releases"]
    os.makedirs(cache_dir(), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    return result


def api_error(product: str, e: Exception) -> str:
    if isinstance(e, UnknownProduct):
        return f"{product}: unknown endoflife.date product"
    if isinstance(e, OSError):
        return f"{product}: endoflife.date API unreachable ({e}), use --offline"
    return f"{product}: bad endoflife.date API response ({e!r})"


def lowest(pin: str) -> str | None:
    """Lowest version in a pin or constraint: `>=3.10,<4` -> `3.10`, `latest` -> None."""
    # ponytail: first number, not the true lower bound (`<4,>=3.10` -> `4`); parse specifiers if that bites
    m = VERSION.search(pin)
    return m.group() if m else None


def to_cycle(version: str, cycles: list[str] | None) -> str:
    """Longest known cycle that `version` belongs to; `major.minor` when offline or unknown."""
    for c in sorted(cycles or (), key=len, reverse=True):
        if version == c or version.startswith(c + "."):

    return ".".join(version.split(".")[:2])

# --- detection ---------------------------------------------------------------


def repo_files(root: str) -> list[str]:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ("git", "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"),
        cwd=root,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout
    return out.splitlines()


def read(root: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(root, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()
    except OSError:
        return None


def first_line(root: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    text = read(root, name)
    return text.strip().splitlines()[0] if text and text.strip() else None


def load_json(root: str, name: str) -> dict:
    try:
        data = json.loads(read(root, name) or "{}")
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}


def load_toml(root: str, name: str) -> dict:
    try:
        return tomllib.loads(read(root, name) or "")
    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
        return {}


def search(pattern: str, text: str | None) -> str | None:
    m = re.search(pattern, text or "", re.MULTILINE)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def tool_pins(root: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Versions pinned in mise.toml / .mise.toml / .tool-versions, keyed by product."""
    pins: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in (read(root, ".tool-versions") or "").splitlines():
        parts = line.split("#")[0].split()
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            pins[parts[0]] = parts[1]
    for name in (".mise.toml", "mise.toml"):  # mise.toml wins
        for tool, value in load_toml(root, name).get("tools", {}).items():
            if isinstance(value, list):
                value = value[0] if value else ""
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                value = value.get("version", "")
            pins[tool] = str(value)
    return {TOOL_ALIASES.get(tool, tool): pin for tool, pin in pins.items()}


def detect(root: str, files: list[str]) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    """Products used in the repo -> their pinned version (None when unpinned)."""
    names = {os.path.basename(f) for f in files}

    def has(*patterns: str) -> bool:
        return any(fnmatch(n, p) for n in names for p in patterns)

    package = load_json(root, "package.json")
    manager = str(package.get("packageManager", ""))
    tf = "\n".join(read(root, f) or "" for f in files if f.endswith(".tf"))
    tools = tool_pins(root)
    found: dict[str, str | None] = {}

    if has("*.py", "pyproject.toml"):
        found["python"] = first_line(root, ".python-version") or load_toml(root, "pyproject.toml").get(
            "project", {}
        ).get("requires-python")
    if "package.json" in names:
        found["nodejs"] = (
            first_line(root, ".nvmrc") or first_line(root, ".node-version") or package.get("engines", {}).get("node")
        )
    for product, lockfiles in (
        ("pnpm", ("pnpm-lock.yaml",)),
        ("yarn", ("yarn.lock",)),
        ("bun", ("bun.lock", "bun.lockb")),
    ):
        if has(*lockfiles):
            found[product] = manager.partition("@")[2] if manager.startswith(product + "@") else None
    if has("deno.json", "deno.jsonc"):
        found["deno"] = None
    if "go.mod" in names:
        found["go"] = search(r"^go\s+(\S+)", read(root, "go.mod"))
    if has("composer.json", "*.php"):
        found["php"] = load_json(root, "composer.json").get("require", {}).get("php")
        found["composer"] = None
    if "pom.xml" in names:
        found["eclipse-temurin"] = search(r"<maven\.compiler\.release>\s*(\d+)", read(root, "pom.xml"))
        found["apache-maven"] = None
    if has("build.gradle", "build.gradle.kts"):
        gradle = (read(root, "build.gradle") or "") + (read(root, "build.gradle.kts") or "")
        found["eclipse-temurin"] = search(r"JavaLanguageVersion\.of\((\d+)\)", gradle)
        found["gradle"] = search(
            r"gradle-(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)-",
            read(root, os.path.join("gradle", "wrapper", "gradle-wrapper.properties")),
        )
    if has("*.tf"):
        tofu = ".opentofu-version" in names or "opentofu" in tools
        found["opentofu" if tofu else "terraform"] = (
            first_line(root, ".opentofu-version") if tofu else None
        ) or search(r'required_version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', tf)
    if "Gemfile" in names:
        found["ruby"] = first_line(root, ".ruby-version")
    if "Cargo.toml" in names:
        found["rust"] = load_toml(root, "rust-toolchain.toml").get("toolchain", {}).get("channel")

    for product in found:
        if lowest(tools.get(product, "")):  # exact mise/asdf pin beats a range like `>= 1.11`
            found[product] = tools[product]
    return found

def parse_products(value: object) -> dict[str, str]:
    """`python@3.12, nodejs@20` -> {"python": "3.12", "nodejs": "20"}."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for item in str(value or "").split(","):
        product, _, cycle = item.strip().partition("@")
        if product:
            out[product.strip()] = cycle.strip()
    return out


def resolve(
    detected: dict[str, str | None], offline: bool, ttl: int, errors: list[str]
) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    """Detected products -> (cycles from repo pins, newest cycles for unpinned products)."""
    pinned: dict[str, str] = {}
    fallback: dict[str, str] = {}
    for product, pin in sorted(detected.items()):
        version = lowest(pin) if pin else None
        try:
            rels = releases(product, ttl, offline)
        except (UnknownProduct, OSError, *BAD_PAYLOAD) as e:
            errors.append(api_error(product, e))
            continue
        if version:
            pinned[product] = to_cycle(version, [r["name"] for r in rels] if rels else None)
        elif rels:
            fallback[product] = latest(rels)
        elif offline:
            click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: {product}: no version pinned and nothing cached, skipped (--offline)")
    return pinned, fallback


def merge(
    existing: dict[str, str], pinned: dict[str, str], fallback: dict[str, str], fixes: list[str]
) -> dict[str, str]:
    products = dict(existing)
    for product, cycle in fallback.items():
        if product not in products:
            products[product] = cycle
            fixes.append(f"added {product}@{cycle} to {ANNOTATION}")
    for product, cycle in pinned.items():
        if product not in products:
            fixes.append(f"added {product}@{cycle} to {ANNOTATION}")
        elif products[product] != cycle:
            fixes.append(f"updated {product}@{products[product]} to {product}@{cycle} (repo pin)")
        products[product] = cycle
    return dict(sorted(products.items()))


def check_cycles(products: dict[str, str], offline: bool, ttl: int, errors: list[str]) -> None:
    for product, cycle in products.items():
        if not cycle:
            errors.append(f"{product}: missing @cycle in {ANNOTATION}")
            continue
        try:
            rels = releases(product, ttl, offline)
        except (UnknownProduct, OSError, *BAD_PAYLOAD) as e:
            errors.append(api_error(product, e))
            continue
        if rels is not None and cycle not in [r["name"] for r in rels]:  # None: offline, nothing cached
            errors.append(f"{product}@{cycle}: unknown cycle, see {API.format(product)}")


def set_annotation(meta: dict, value: str) -> None:
    annotations = meta.get("annotations")
    if annotations is None:
        keys = list(meta)
        after = max(keys.index(k) for k in ("name", "namespace", "title", "description") if k in keys)
        meta.insert(after + 1, "annotations", {ANNOTATION: value})
    else:
        annotations[ANNOTATION] = value

def main(offline: bool, cache_ttl: int) -> int:
    """Checks and fixes the repo's Backstage catalog-info.yaml."""
    root = project_dir()
    path = os.path.join(root, CATALOG)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: not found in {root}")
        sys.exit(1)

    fixes: list[str] = []
    errors: list[str] = []
    prelude, body = split_prelude(text)
    if not any(
        "yaml-language-server:" in line for line in takewhile(lambda line: line.startswith("#"), prelude.splitlines())
    ):
        prelude = HEADER + "\n" + prelude
        fixes.append("added yaml-language-server header")

    y = yaml_rt()
    y.explicit_start = body.lstrip().startswith("---")
    try:
        docs = list(y.load_all(body))
    except YAMLError as e:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    if all(doc is None for doc in docs):
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: no entities")
        sys.exit(1)

    resolved = None
    dirty = False  # body re-dumped only when an entity changed, so valid files stay byte-identical
    for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
        if doc is None:  # empty document, e.g. a trailing `---`
            continue
        meta = doc.get("metadata") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not meta.get("name"):
            errors.append(f"document {i}: metadata.name is required")
            continue
        if "namespace" not in meta:
            meta.insert(list(meta).index("name") + 1, "namespace", "default")
            fixes.append(f"{meta['name']}: added metadata.namespace: default")
            dirty = True
        if doc.get("kind") not in EOL_KINDS:
            continue
        if resolved is None:  # detection and API lookups only when an entity needs them
            resolved = resolve(detect(root, repo_files(root)), offline, cache_ttl, errors)
        current = (meta.get("annotations") or {}).get(ANNOTATION)
        fixes_before, errors_before = len(fixes), len(errors)
        products = merge(parse_products(current), *resolved, fixes)
        check_cycles(products, offline, cache_ttl, errors)
        if len(errors) > errors_before:  # never write an annotation we know is invalid
            del fixes[fixes_before:]
            continue
        value = ",".join(f"{p}@{c}" for p, c in products.items())
        if value and value != current:
            if len(fixes) == fixes_before:
                fixes.append(f"normalized {ANNOTATION}")
            fixes[fixes_before:] = [f"{meta['name']}: {fix}" for fix in fixes[fixes_before:]]
            set_annotation(meta, value)
            dirty = True

    if dirty:
        out = io.StringIO()
        y.dump_all([doc for doc in docs if doc is not None], out)  # ruamel writes empty docs as `...`
        body = out.getvalue()
    if fixes:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(prelude + body)
    for message in fixes + errors:
        click.echo(f"{CATALOG}: {message}")
    sys.exit(1 if fixes or errors else 0)

# check-catalog-info

Makes sure the repository has a valid Backstage `catalog-info.yaml` at its
root and fixes what it can: the schema header, `metadata.namespace` and the
[endoflife.date](https://endoflife.date) `endoflife.date/products` annotation.
Like `end-of-file-fixer`, it fails the commit when it changed the file, so you
review and stage the fix.

## Usage

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/DimkaGorhover/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: <commit-sha>
    hooks:
      - id: check-catalog-info
```

Runs on every commit (`always_run`, no filenames) on the `pre-commit`,
`pre-push` and `manual` stages.

??? info "Hook definition"

    ```yaml
    - id: check-catalog-info
      name: check Backstage catalog-info.yaml
      description: >-
        requires a root catalog-info.yaml with a schema header, metadata.name and
        metadata.namespace, and keeps its endoflife.date/products annotation in sync
        with the languages and tools used in the repo.
      entry: check-catalog-info
      language: python
      always_run: true
      pass_filenames: false
      stages:
        - pre-commit
        - pre-push
        - manual
    ```

## How it works

- Fails when `catalog-info.yaml` is missing, does not parse, or has no
    entities.
- Adds
    `# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/catalog-info.json`
    when the leading comment block has no `yaml-language-server` header. Pair
    it with [check-yaml-schema](check-yaml-schema.md) to validate against the
    schema.
- Every entity needs `metadata.name`; a missing `metadata.namespace` becomes
    `namespace: default`.
- For `Component` and `Resource` entities the `endoflife.date/products`
    annotation (`product@cycle,...`, sorted) is kept in sync with the repo:
    - products are detected from files tracked by git (`*.py` → `python`,
        `package.json` → `nodejs`, lockfiles → `pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun`, `go.mod` →
        `go`, `composer.json`/`*.php` → `php` + `composer`, `pom.xml` →
        `eclipse-temurin` + `apache-maven`, `build.gradle(.kts)` →
        `eclipse-temurin` + `gradle`, `*.tf` → `terraform` or `opentofu`,
        `Gemfile` → `ruby`, `Cargo.toml` → `rust`, `deno.json` → `deno`);
    - the cycle comes from a repo pin: `mise.toml` / `.tool-versions` first,
        then `.python-version`, `requires-python`, `.nvmrc`, `engines.node`,
        `packageManager`, `go.mod`, `require.php`, `required_version`, ...;
    - a pinned cycle that differs from the annotation is rewritten;
    - an unpinned product gets the newest non-EOL cycle, but only when it is
        missing from the annotation;
    - products the hook cannot detect (e.g. `gitlab@19.3`) are kept;
    - every `product@cycle` is checked against
        `https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/<product>/`.
- API responses are cached in `$TMPDIR/pre-commit-hooks-endoflife/`. A stale
    entry is still used when the API is unreachable. On Linux `$TMPDIR` is
    often the shared `/tmp`, so other local users could pre-seed it; that only
    affects which cycles the hook accepts.
- A file that is already valid is never rewritten; when it is, comments,
    quoting and folded scalars are preserved.

## Example

```console
$ prek run check-catalog-info
check Backstage catalog-info.yaml........................................Failed
- hook id: check-catalog-info
- exit code: 1
- files were modified by this hook

catalog-info.yaml: terraform-gitlab: added metadata.namespace: default
catalog-info.yaml: updated terraform@1.15 to terraform@1.16 (repo pin)
```

## Options

| Option        | Default | Description                                                         |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--offline`   | off     | No API calls: repo pins plus any cached API response; unpinned products with nothing cached are skipped |
| `--cache-ttl` | `86400` | Seconds an endoflife.date API response stays cached                 |

    ```sh
    pre-commit run check-catalog-info --all-files
    ```

=== "Directly"

    ```sh
    check-catalog-info [--offline] [--cache-ttl SECONDS]
    ```

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: A pre-commit hook (run via prek) that makes sure a repo has a valid Backstage catalog-info.yaml at its root, auto-fixing what it can and failing the commit when it changed something or found something it cannot fix (like end-of-file-fixer).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Only <git-root>/catalog-info.yaml. Nested catalog files are out of scope.
  • Every YAML document in the file is checked for metadata.name / metadata.namespace.
  • Only kind: Component and kind: Resource documents get the endoflife.date/products annotation.
  • Dockerfiles are not scanned.
  • JSON-schema validation is not repeated here; check-yaml-schema covers it once the header exists.

docs.title: Hook surface
docs.text:
• id / entry: check-catalog-info, language: python, always_run: true, pass_filenames: false, stages pre-commit, pre-push, manual.
  • Registered in pyproject.toml [project.scripts] and .pre-commit-hooks.yaml; doc page docs/hooks/check-catalog-info.md (added to mkdocs nav like the other hooks).
  • New dependencies: ruamel.yaml, and tomli on Python 3.10 (no tomllib).
  • Flags:
    • --offline: no API calls; cycles come from pins and cached API responses.
    • --cache-ttl SECONDS: API cache freshness, default 86400.
  • Exit code: 0 when the file is valid and unchanged; 1 when it was fixed (each fix printed) or an unfixable problem was found.
  • Code: single module pre_commit_hooks/check_catalog_info.py, tests in tests/check_catalog_info_test.py.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. Read <git-root>/catalog-info.yaml (root via util.project_dir()). Missing → error catalog-info.yaml not found.
  2. Split the file into a prelude (leading # and blank lines) and the body (the rest). ruamel drops comments before the first ---, so the prelude is handled as plain text.
    • No yaml-language-server: line in the first comment block (up to the first non-# line, like check-yaml-schema) → prepend # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/catalog-info.json.
    • A yaml-language-server: line with another schema is left untouched.
  3. Round-trip the body with ruamel: YAML(), preserve_quotes = True, indent(mapping=2, sequence=4, offset=2), width = 4096, explicit_start matching the source. Verified to reproduce the body of the four sample TNET catalog files byte-for-byte. The body is re-dumped only when an entity changed, so a valid file is never rewritten. Empty documents (e.g. a trailing ---) are skipped and dropped on rewrite; a file with no entities at all is an error.
  4. For each document:
    • metadata.name missing → error.
    • metadata.namespace missing → insert namespace: default right after name.
  5. For each Component / Resource document, rebuild metadata.annotations["endoflife.date/products"]:
    • Parse the existing value: comma-separated product@cycle, whitespace trimmed.
    • Detect products in the repo (table below) and resolve each one's cycle.
    • Merge:
      • detected product missing from the annotation → add it;
      • detected product whose cycle comes from a repo pin and differs → rewrite to the pinned cycle (repo pin is the source of truth);
      • detected but unpinned product already in the annotation → keep its cycle (the API's newest cycle only fills in missing products);
      • product only in the annotation (e.g. gitlab@19.3) → keep as is.
    • Validate every resulting product@cycle against the API (offline: against the cache when there is one). If any is invalid the annotation is reported and left untouched, never rewritten.
    • Write the value sorted by product name, joined with ,. Create annotations: if absent. Nothing detected and no existing value → no annotation written.
  6. If the content changed, write prelude + body back, print each fix, exit 1.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
Files come from git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard (tracked plus new untracked files; ignored dirs like node_modules, .venv, .terraform are skipped). Detection matches files anywhere in the repo, but pin files (.python-version, package.json, go.mod, ...) are read from the repo root only; the exception is required_version, taken from the first *.tf anywhere in the repo that sets it.

Detected by Product(s) Cycle from (first hit wins) *.py, pyproject.toml python .python-version, requires-python package.json nodejs .nvmrc / .node-version, engines.node pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock / bun.lock, bun.lockb pnpm / yarn / bun packageManager in package.json deno.json, deno.jsonc deno — go.mod go go directive composer.json, *.php php, composer require.php (php) pom.xml eclipse-temurin, apache-maven maven.compiler.release (temurin) build.gradle, build.gradle.kts eclipse-temurin, gradle toolchain languageVersion (temurin), gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties (gradle) *.tf terraform, or opentofu if .opentofu-version exists or mise pins opentofu required_version Gemfile ruby .ruby-version Cargo.toml rust rust-toolchain.toml

An exact pin in mise.toml / .mise.toml [tools] or .tool-versions overrides the product-specific source (tool name = product name, plus node → nodejs, java → eclipse-temurin, maven → apache-maven): it is what actually runs, while required_version = ">= 1.11" is only a floor. Without a usable mise pin (latest, lts, missing) the table's source is used. Still nothing → newest non-EOL cycle from the API. In --offline mode an unpinned product is reported as skipped and not added.

docs.title: Cycle normalization
docs.text:
• A version or constraint (3.12.4, ^3.12, >=3.10,<4, ~> 1.16.0, v20.11.0) is reduced to its lowest bound (3.12.4, 3.12, 3.10, 1.16.0, 20.11.0).
  • The cycle is the longest cycle name from the product's API list that is equal to the version or a dot-prefix of it (3.12.4 → 3.12 for python, 20.11.0 → 20 for nodejs).
  • Offline: fall back to major.minor (or major when that is all there is).
  • latest / lts (mise) count as no pin.

docs.title: endoflife.date API and cache
docs.text:
• GET https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/<product>/ via urllib, 30s timeout; cycles are result.releases[].name, EOL from result.releases[].isEol.
  • Cache: $TMPDIR/pre-commit-hooks-endoflife/<product>.json (tempfile.gettempdir()), fresh while its mtime is younger than --cache-ttl. Stale or missing → fetch and overwrite; if the fetch fails, a stale entry is used anyway. --offline uses any cache entry regardless of age and never fetches; only without one does it fall back to major.minor and skip unpinned products.
  • HTTP 404 → unknown product (error). Network failure → error suggesting --offline.
  • Product names must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.+-]*$ before they are used in the URL or the cache path; anything else is an unknown product.

docs.title: Errors (fail, no fix)
docs.text:
• catalog-info.yaml not found
  • YAML parse error
  • no entities in the file
  • metadata.name missing (reported per document index)
  • unknown product in the annotation
  • cycle not in the product's API cycle list
  • API unreachable (online mode)
  • product without @cycle in the annotation

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
pytest, each case a tmp_path git repo; the cache dir is pointed at a fixture dir pre-seeded with product JSON so tests never hit the network.

  • missing file fails
  • header added; existing non-catalog header kept
  • namespace: default inserted in every document of a multi-doc file
  • missing metadata.name fails
  • Location-only file gets no annotation
  • detection + pin resolution: python, nodejs + pnpm, go, php + composer, terraform from mise.toml
  • stale cycle rewritten; annotation-only product kept
  • invalid cycle and unknown product fail
  • annotation output sorted
  • second run is a no-op (idempotence)
  • file shaped like terraform-gitlab/catalog-info.yaml already valid → unchanged byte-for-byte
  • stale cache entry is refetched (TTL)
